about: At “Nobis quoque peccatóribus” the rubric directs the priest to raise his voice a little and strike his breast. The prayer asks that God’s sinful servants be admitted to fellowship with the Saints.

seg.nr: The priest strikes his breast with his right hand and says, with his voice raised a little:
The priest spreads his hands as before and goes on silently.

seg.tr: Your servants, who hope in the multitude of Your mercies, be pleased to grant some part and fellowship with Your holy Apostles and Martyrs:

ex.w006: The idiom “speráre de” names the ground of hope rather than a place: we hope on the strength of the multitude of God’s mercies.

seg.tr: with John, Stephen, Matthias, Barnabas, Ignatius, Alexander, Marcellinus, Peter, Felicity, Perpetua, Agatha, Lucy, Agnes, Cecilia, Anastasia, and all Your saints:

ex.w031: Peter the Exorcist, Marcellinus’s companion in martyrdom — not the Apostle.

seg.tr: admit us into their company, we ask You, not as one who weighs merit, but as one who freely grants pardon.

ex.w048: Stands in the nominative beside the imperative “admítte” (w054): the title names the unexpressed “you” of the plea, parallel to “largítor” (w053).
ex.w053: Like “æstimátor” (w048), a nominative title for the unexpressed “you” of “admítte” (w054).

ex.w058: No “Amen” follows here: the Canon does not close but flows on into “Per quem hæc ómnia”.
